context: Round 2 re-runs skills-freshness A/B after PR #18 tightened the SKILL.md with `limit=80`, `no deep read`, `one ls per finding, max 3 traces total, don't spelunk` guidance. Validates whether the three mechanisms identified in Round 1's forensic pass actually translate to per-cell savings.

skill_md_diff.step_3_unchanged_row: Read the SKILL.md once. Verify: (a)..., (b)..., (c)... Surface anything off.
skill_md_diff.step_3_post_fix_row: Read the SKILL.md once with `limit=80` (frontmatter + first one or two sections is all you need — no deep read). Verify: (a)..., (b)..., (c) no broken file/command references in the body — cap path verification at one `ls` per finding, max 3 traces total, don't spelunk into source repos. Surface anything off.

sonnet.interpretation: Still positive but smaller magnitude. The BEFORE cost dropped 195K -> 106K — sonnet's cold scan became cheaper on this run (likely cache state and a different traversal strategy). N=1 variance; sign and direction unchanged.

opus.interpretation: Sign-flip cleared. The `max 3 traces total, don't spelunk` cap killed the 4-Bash-call source-repo hunt that drove Round 1's -21%. Post-fix sits at break-even — the procedural overhead and procedural savings are now roughly balanced.

haiku.interpretation: Largest swing in the study (+90pp). The `limit=80, no deep read` guidance killed the 233K-char full-file read pattern. Haiku BEFORE actually grew 64K -> 97K (the model decided to read more on the cold pass this time), AFTER stayed similar to Round 1, so the relative save flipped strongly positive.

hypothesis_verdict: CONFIRMED. All three skills-freshness cells now net-positive (was 1 of 3 in Round 1). The three mechanisms identified by the forensic pass are real and the SKILL.md fixes neutralise them.

epistemic_notes.controls_for_model_drift: yes — Round 2 ran ~25 minutes after Round 1's data
epistemic_notes.skills_quality_not_remeasured: skills-quality SKILL.md was unchanged by the fix (it was already clean by its own rules); re-measuring those 3 cells would have added noise without testable signal
epistemic_notes.sonnet_regression_explained: Sonnet's +43% -> +14% is mostly BEFORE-arm variance: the cold scan happened to take a different (cheaper) route this time. AFTER-arm token cost barely moved (111K -> 91K). The optimization still saves, just less relative to a now-cheaper baseline.
